name: IF

args.name: test
args.about: something that is TRUE or FALSE, like B2>100

args.name: value_if_true
args.about: what to show when it's TRUE

args.name: value_if_false
args.about: what to show when it's FALSE (FALSE if left out)

about: Shows one thing when a test is TRUE and another when it's FALSE.

example.why: 120 is more than 100, so the test is TRUE.

name: AND

args.name: logical1
args.about: a test, like B2>0, or cells holding TRUE or FALSE

args.name: logical2
args.about: more tests

about: Gives TRUE only when every test is TRUE.

example.why: Ann is over 18 and is a member, so both tests are TRUE.

notes: OR gives TRUE when any test is TRUE.

example.why: It always gives FALSE; typing FALSE on its own does the same.

name: IFERROR

args.name: value
args.about: the formula or cell to check

args.name: value_if_error
args.about: what to show if it is an error

about: Shows a value unless it's an error, in which case it shows something else.

example.why: 300 divided by 0 is the error #DIV/0!, so the fallback text is shown.

notes: IFNA only catches #N/A and lets other errors through.

name: IFNA

args.name: value
args.about: the formula or cell to check

args.name: value_if_na
args.about: what to show if it is #N/A

about: Shows a value unless it's #N/A, in which case it shows something else.

example.why: There is no Plum, so VLOOKUP gives #N/A and the fallback text is shown.

notes: IFERROR catches every kind of error.

name: IFS

args.name: test1
args.about: the first test

args.name: value1
args.about: what to show when the first test is TRUE

args.name: test2
args.about: the next test

args.name: value2
args.about: what to show when that test is TRUE

about: Goes through tests in order and shows the value for the first one that is TRUE.

example.why: 72 is not 80 or more, but it is 70 or more, so the second value is shown.

notes: Gives #N/A when no test is TRUE; put TRUE as the last test to catch everything else.

name: LAMBDA

args.name: parameter1
args.about: a name for a value the function takes

args.name: calculation
args.about: the formula worked out with those names; always last

about: Makes your own function out of a formula, with names for the values it takes.

example.why: The function adds the rate to the price, and is called straight away with 50 and 0.2: 50 × 1.2 = 60.

notes: A LAMBDA that isn't called gives #CALC!. Give it to MAP, REDUCE, BYROW and the like, or call it with values in brackets after it.

name: LET

args.name: name1
args.about: a name for a value

args.name: value1
args.about: the value that name stands for

args.name: calculation
args.about: the formula using the names; always last

about: Gives names to values inside a formula, so each is worked out once and the formula reads better.

name: NOT

args.name: logical
args.about: a test or value that is TRUE or FALSE

about: Turns TRUE into FALSE and FALSE into TRUE.

example.why: The task isn't done, so NOT turns FALSE into TRUE.

name: OR

args.name: logical1
args.about: a test, like B2>0, or cells holding TRUE or FALSE

args.name: logical2
args.about: more tests

about: Gives TRUE when at least one test is TRUE.

example.why: The day is Sat, so the first test is TRUE.

notes: AND needs every test to be TRUE; XOR needs an odd number of them.

name: SWITCH

args.name: expression
args.about: the value to compare

args.name: value1
args.about: the first value to match

args.name: result1
args.about: what to show when it matches

args.name: default_or_value2
args.about: what to show when nothing matches, or the next value to match

about: Compares a value with a list and shows the result paired with the one it matches.

example.why: B2 holds M, which is paired with Medium.

notes: Gives #N/A when nothing matches and there is no default at the end.

example.why: It always gives TRUE; typing TRUE on its own does the same.

name: XOR

args.name: logical1
args.about: a test, or cells holding TRUE or FALSE

args.name: logical2
args.about: more tests

about: Gives TRUE when an odd number of the tests are TRUE, so with two tests, when exactly one is.

example.why: Sam likes both, so two tests are TRUE, an even number.

name: BYCOL

args.name: array
args.about: the cells to go through column by column

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking one column and giving one value

about: Works out one value for each column of a range, using a LAMBDA.

example.why: The Jan column adds up to 10 + 5 = 15; 35 and 55 for Feb and Mar spill to the right.

name: BYROW

args.name: array
args.about: the cells to go through row by row

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking one row and giving one value

about: Works out one value for each row of a range, using a LAMBDA.

example.why: Ann's best quarter is 60; Ben's 30 spills into the cell below.

name: MAP

args.name: array1
args.about: the cells to go through one by one

args.name: array2
args.about: more ranges of the same size, taken alongside

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking one value from each range; always last

about: Works out a new value for every cell of a range, using a LAMBDA.

example.why: 10 doubled is 20; 50 and 80 spill into the cells below.

name: REDUCE

args.name: initial_value
args.about: the starting value

args.name: array
args.about: the cells to go through one by one

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking the value so far and the next cell, giving the new value so far

about: Goes through a range carrying a running value, and gives the final value.
notes: SCAN gives every value along the way instead of just the last.

name: SCAN

args.name: initial_value
args.about: the starting value

args.name: array
args.about: the cells to go through one by one

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking the value so far and the next cell, giving the new value so far

about: Goes through a range carrying a running value, and gives the value after each cell, like a running total.

example.why: The running total after the first month is 120; 200 and 350 spill into the cells below.

notes: REDUCE gives only the final value.

name: MAKEARRAY

args.name: rows
args.about: how many rows

args.name: columns
args.about: how many columns

args.name: lambda
args.about: a LAMBDA taking the row and column number, giving the value for that cell

about: Builds a block of values of a given size, working out each one with a LAMBDA.

example.why: Row 1 times column 1 is 1; the rest of a 3 by 3 times table spills right and down.
